meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.en: immediately, on the spot, right this second
meanings.note: often paired with 지금 (지금 당장) for strong emphasis

examples.trans: Try calling right away.
We have to start right this second.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 당황스럽다 정말, 넌 그래서 배꼽 잡겠냐?
examples.trans: Now I am the one flustered—would that make you laugh your head off?
This expression comes from 'is baffling'.

meanings.note: Used as present adnominal (대답하는).

examples.text: 시간을 좀 드릴게요. 피디님이 당황스러울 테니까 지금 당장 대답하는 건 좀 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.trans: I will give you some time—you must be flustered, so answering right on the spot does not seem right.
Is that an interrogation—am I obligated to answer you?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

examples.text: 너 지금 경합이 무슨 뜻인지 알고 그런 소리 하니?
examples.trans: Do you even know what competition means when you say that?
The topic of what meaning it is came up during this shoot.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Standard polite negative reply.

examples.trans: No, I'm okay.
No, I haven't eaten yet.

meanings.note: Usually followed by a negative verb to mean 'nobody' or 'nothing'.

examples.trans: Nobody is here.
Please give me anything.

meanings.note: Contracted form of 이야기하다

examples.trans: Let's talk again later.
Please tell me honestly.

meanings.note: Used as acronym noun + polite copula (MC예요?).

examples.text: 나 MC예요? 왜 나 혼자 진행을 하고 있어?
examples.trans: Am I a show host here? Why am I hosting this whole conversation by myself?
This point about am I an emcee is really important.
Did you hear about this several?
I was busy today because of several.
Did you hear about this celebrity?
I was busy today because of celebrity.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 좀 더 자숙하는 의미로 한복 입고 가면 어떨까?
examples.trans: To show deeper self-reflection, how about wearing traditional Korean attire?
Here the word for 'as a gesture of' is key.

이러다.gloss: to do this, to act like this

meanings.en: to do this, to act like this
meanings.note: Contracted from 이러하다.

examples.trans: Why are you acting like this?
Please don't do this.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Used as noun (정리).

examples.text: 제가 좀 이렇게 정리 안 된 걸 잘 못 보는 성격이라.
examples.trans: My personality is the sort that cannot stand seeing things untidy like this.
This point about tidying, order is really important.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금

examples.trans: Test
Test2
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (진행을).

examples.text: 나 MC예요? 왜 나 혼자 진행을 하고 있어?
examples.trans: Am I a show host here? Why am I hosting this whole conversation by myself?
This point about hosting, running things is really important.

meanings.note: 처음부터 means 'from the start'

examples.trans: Let's start over from the beginning.
This is my first time coming to Seoul.
Did you hear about this since I intend to?
I was busy today because of since I intend to.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.
I want to even try right now.
How about trying to even try together tomorrow?
I ate alone today.
I can do it well by myself too.

meanings.note: Can also function as a noun
